title: When things go wrong
cando: tell what happened and what was going on at the time

about.text: In this lesson things go wrong on the way to work. You tell a colleague what happened, and what was going on at the time. Then you read an incident record, and you phone your manager about a problem.
goals: Tell a story, and react to one: You'll never guess what happened! Oh no!
Say what was going on: I was waiting when the call came.
Use past forms like taught, spent and hid.
Read an incident record and a witness statement. Write about a morning that went wrong.
Phone your manager about a problem, then fill in the incident record.

chapters.title: You'll never guess what happened
chapters.text:
In this lesson things go wrong, and you tell people what happened.
First, you listen to Omar. He arrives at work very late, and his colleague Lena asks why.
Omar says: You'll never guess what happened! This tells Lena that a surprising story is coming.
Lena asks: What happened then? When the news is bad, she says: Oh no!
Listen to the end of the past verbs. Crashed ends in a t sound. Realised ends in a d sound. Waited has one more part: wait-ed.

chapters.title: What was going on, and what happened
chapters.text:
In a story, one thing is often going on already. Then something happens in the middle of it.
For the thing that was going on, use was or were, and an -ing verb. I was waiting for the bus.
For the thing that happened, use the past. The call came.
Join them with when. I was waiting when the call came.
Or start with while. While I was waiting, the call came.
Some past forms do not end in -ed. Teach becomes taught. Spend becomes spent. Hide becomes hid. Learn them in pairs, out loud.

chapters.title: An incident record
chapters.text:
Next, you read two short documents from a workplace.
An incident record is a form. It says what happened, when and where, and what the staff did.
A witness statement is one person's own words about what they saw.
Read both. What do they both say? What does only one of them say?
Then you write about a morning that went wrong. Tell the events in order.

chapters.title: A call to your manager
chapters.text:
In the task, you have a problem on the way to work. You phone your manager.
Say sorry first. Then say where you are, and what happened.
Say what you were doing: I was sitting on the bus when it stopped.
Say when you will probably arrive. Then, at work, you fill in the incident record.

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a story or an article about a day when things went wrong.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again and answer the questions.

warmup.prompt: You are on your way to work, and the road is closed. What do you do first?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. Many people call or send a message first. Then the manager knows, and nobody worries.

conversation.title: You'll never guess what happened!
conversation.setting: It is Monday morning. Omar arrives at the office forty minutes late. His colleague Lena sees him by the lift.
lines: Morning, Omar! Is everything OK? You're very late.
I know. Sorry I'm late! You'll never guess what happened.
I was sitting on the bus when it suddenly stopped. There were roadworks on the main road.
The driver took a detour, but we spent half an hour in a traffic jam.
Well, while we were waiting, I realised my phone was at home!
A bit. And then the man next to me spilled his coffee on my bag.
I was, but he was very sorry. Luckily, my laptop was OK.
Well, I'm relieved you're here. The meeting starts in five minutes.
Then I'll get a coffee first. I didn't have one this morning!

questions.a: There were roadworks on the main road.
wrong: There was a crash on the main road.
questions.why: Omar says: There were roadworks on the main road.

questions.q: What was happening when Omar realised his phone was at home?
questions.a: They were waiting in a traffic jam.
wrong: He was walking to the office.
questions.why: Omar says: While we were waiting, I realised my phone was at home!

questions.q: What did the man next to Omar do?
questions.a: He spilled his coffee on Omar's bag.
questions.why: Omar says: The man next to me spilled his coffee on my bag.

phrases.use: Saying sorry when you arrive late.
Asking for the next part of a story.
Saying the good part of a bad story.
Saying you were worried, but now you are not.

items.meaning: A long queue of cars and buses on a road. They can't move, or they move very slowly.
items.example: We sat in a traffic jam for forty minutes.

items.meaning: Work to repair a road. Part of the road is closed.
items.example: There are roadworks on the main road until Friday.

items.meaning: A longer way to go, because the usual road is closed.
items.example: The bus took a detour around the roadworks.

items.meaning: The way a bus, a train or a person goes from one place to another.
items.example: What's the quickest route to the station?

items.meaning: To make a drink fall out of its cup by accident. The past is spilled or spilt.
items.example: I spilled coffee on my keyboard.

items.meaning: To hit something hard, like a car hitting a wall. A computer can crash too: it suddenly stops working.
items.example: My computer crashed, and I lost the report.

items.meaning: To suddenly understand or notice something.
items.example: At the station, I realised my wallet was at home.

items.meaning: To feel so afraid or worried that you can't think clearly. The past is panicked.
items.example: Don't panic. The next train is in ten minutes.

items.meaning: A little angry.
items.example: I was annoyed because the bus was late again.

items.meaning: Happy because a worry or a problem has gone.
items.example: I was relieved when I found my keys.

items.meaning: Sad or worried because something bad happened.
items.example: She was upset about the mistake in her report.

items.meaning: Feeling that something happened that you did not expect.
items.example: I was surprised to see my old boss on the train.

items.meaning: It is good that this happened.
items.example: Luckily, nobody was hurt.

items.meaning: Now, at once, with no wait.
items.example: Call your manager immediately.

sound.title: The -ed ending
sound.explain: The -ed ending has three sounds. After sounds like k, p, s, sh and ch, it sounds like t: crashed, panicked. After most other sounds, it sounds like d: realised, spilled. After t and d, it adds one more part: wait-ed. Listen, then say each group.
lines: I realised my phone was at home.
We waited for half an hour.

sayIt.instructions: Say Omar's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Can you hear the end of each past verb?
lines: I was sitting on the bus when it suddenly stopped. There were roadworks on the main road.
The driver took a detour, but we spent half an hour in a traffic jam.
Well, while we were waiting, I realised my phone was at home!
A bit. And then the man next to me spilled his coffee on my bag.

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation. The first two have two parts: something that was going on, and something that happened.
examples: I was sitting on the bus when it suddenly stopped.
While we were waiting, I realised my phone was at home.
We spent half an hour in a traffic jam.
spot.question: In the first two sentences, which part was going on already? Which part happened in the middle of it? And what is the past of spend?
spot.answer: Was sitting and were waiting were going on already: was or were + -ing. It stopped and I realised happened in the middle: the past. Spend becomes spent. It does not add -ed.

rules.title: I was waiting when the call came
rule: Going on already: was or were + -ing. I was waiting. We were talking.
Happened in the middle: the past. The call came. The bus stopped.
Join them with when: I was waiting when the call came.
Or put while before the long part: While I was waiting, the call came.
Ask: What were you doing at the time? — I was driving to work.
rules.mistake: Not: I was wait when the call came. Say: I was waiting when the call came.

rules.title: Past forms to learn: taught, spent, hid
rule: Some verbs do not add -ed in the past. Learn them in pairs, out loud.
teach – taught, spend – spent, hide – hid
throw – threw, wear – wore, fall – fell
She taught me the job. We spent an hour there. A van hid the sign.
After did and didn't, use the plain verb: Did she teach you? I didn't fall.
rules.mistake: Not: She teached me the job. Say: She taught me the job.

practice.q: I ___ dinner when the lights went off.
They ___ talking when the manager came in.
While I ___ to work, I saw an accident.
practice.why: The long part after while: was + -ing.

practice.q: I was waiting at the bus stop when my manager ___ .
practice.why: The short event: the past, called.

practice.q: What ___ you doing at nine o'clock? — I was driving to work.
practice.why: Asking what was going on: What were you doing?

practice.q: My first manager ___ me how to use the machine.
We ___ two hours at the hospital yesterday.
A big van ___ the sign, so I didn't see it.
I slipped on the wet floor and ___ .
Did you ___ a helmet at work yesterday?
practice.why: After did, use the plain verb: wear.

yourTurn.prompt: Think of a time when something went wrong. It can be at work, at home or on a journey. Write three sentences. Say what was going on, and what happened. Use when or while.
yourTurn.model: I was cooking dinner when the lights went off. While I was looking for a torch, I fell over a chair. Luckily, my neighbour had some candles.

text.title: An incident record and a witness statement
text.body:
PRACTICE FORM: this company does not exist.
KELLWAY FOODS · INCIDENT RECORD
Record number: 27
Date: Tuesday 10 March · Time: 8.40 am
Place: ground floor corridor, by the kitchen doorway
Written by: Mei Chen, supervisor
WHAT HAPPENED: A cleaner was washing the corridor floor. Samir Haddad was coming out of the kitchen with a hot drink. He slipped on the wet floor and fell. He hurt his arm.
CAUSE: The wet floor sign was behind the kitchen door, so nobody could see it.
WHAT WE DID: First aid at 8.45. At 8.50 the floor was dry, and the situation was safe. Samir went home at 10.00.
WITNESS DETAILS: Kwame Mensah, receptionist
NEXT TIME: Put the sign in the doorway before you wash a floor. Write a report on the same day.

- - - - - - - -

WITNESS STATEMENT
Name: Kwame Mensah · Job: receptionist
I was walking along the corridor to the lift at about 8.40. Samir was coming out of the kitchen with a cup of tea. Suddenly he slipped and fell. His tea went all over the floor.
I didn't see a sign, but the floor was very wet. I helped Samir to a chair and called the supervisor immediately.
Samir was upset, but he could move his arm.
Signed: K. Mensah

gist.a: A man slipped on a wet floor.
wrong: A cleaner fell down the stairs.
A man dropped a box on his foot.
gist.why: The record says: He slipped on the wet floor and fell.

gist.a: a person who saw Samir fall
gist.why: Kwame was walking along the corridor, and he saw Samir slip and fall.

detail.q: What was the cause of the incident?
detail.a: Nobody could see the wet floor sign.
detail.why: The record says the sign was behind the kitchen door, so nobody could see it.

detail.q: What was Kwame doing when Samir fell?
detail.a: He was walking to the lift.
wrong: He was making tea in the kitchen.
detail.why: Kwame says: I was walking along the corridor to the lift.
Kwame says: I called the supervisor immediately.

detail.q: What must staff do next time?
detail.a: Put the sign in the doorway before washing a floor.
wrong: Carry hot drinks in the lift.
detail.why: The record says: Put the sign in the doorway before you wash a floor.

items.meaning: Something bad or unusual that happens, for example at work.
items.example: Please tell your supervisor about every incident.

items.meaning: A person who sees something happen, like an accident.
items.example: Were there any witnesses?

items.meaning: What a person says or writes about something that happened.
items.example: The witness wrote a short statement.

items.meaning: A piece of writing that tells people what happened.
items.example: I wrote a report about the incident.

items.meaning: The thing that makes something happen.
items.example: The cause of the delay was the roadworks.

items.meaning: One small piece of information.
items.example: Write down every detail: the time, the place and the names.

items.meaning: A long, narrow space inside a building, with doors to rooms.
items.example: The toilets are at the end of the corridor.

items.meaning: The space where a door opens into a room.
items.example: Please don't leave boxes in the doorway.

items.meaning: To slide by accident on something wet, and often fall.
items.example: I slipped on the wet floor and hurt my back.

items.meaning: What is happening at one time and in one place.
items.example: The situation was difficult, but everyone stayed calm.

model.title: A morning that went wrong
model.body:
Last Friday was a bad morning.
I was eating breakfast when I realised the time. It was already 8.15!
I ran to the bus stop, but the bus was leaving. The next one came at 8.40.
While I was sitting on the bus, it started to rain. Then I realised my umbrella was at home.
I arrived at work at 9.20, and I was very wet.
Luckily, my manager just laughed. She gave me a towel and a hot coffee.

write.task: Write about a morning that went wrong. It can be real or made up. Put the events in order, and say what was going on at the time.
write.starter: Last … was a bad morning. I was …
checklist: I used was or were + -ing for something that was going on.
I joined two parts with when or while.
I put the events in order, with then or luckily.
I said how I felt: annoyed, relieved, upset …

card.title: Late for work
card.situation: It is 8.30 on Monday morning, and you are on the bus to work. There is a crash on the main road, so the bus is taking a detour. You will be about 40 minutes late. Your shift starts at 9.00.
card.goal: Phone your manager. Say where you are, what happened and what you were doing at the time. Say when you will probably arrive. Then, at work, fill in the incident record.

phrases: Hi, it's … . I'm sorry, but I'm going to be late.
I was sitting on the bus when it suddenly stopped.
There was a crash on the main road, so the bus is taking a detour.
I'll probably be there at about twenty to ten.
Do I need to fill in an incident record?
prepare.notes: Make notes. Where were you? What were you doing? What happened? When will you arrive? Then write three lines for the record: the time, the place and what happened.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher is your manager. Phone and explain the problem, and answer the questions. Then fill in the incident record, and read it aloud.
doIt.wehel: You are my manager at work. I am phoning you because I am going to be late. Ask me: Where are you? What happened? What were you doing at the time? When will you arrive? Then help me fill in an incident record: the date, the time, the place and what happened. Use simple English.

model.title: The phone call and the record
lines: Hi Ana, it's Carlos. I'm sorry, but I'm going to be late.
I was sitting on the bus when it suddenly stopped. There was a crash on the main road.
Yes, luckily nobody was hurt. But the road is closed, so the bus is taking a detour.
I see. When do you think you'll get here?
I'll probably be there at about twenty to ten.
OK. Thanks for calling me immediately.
Do I need to fill in an incident record?
Yes, please. Write the time, the place and what happened.
Monday, 8.30 am, Mill Road. I was on the number 12 bus when a car crashed. The road was closed, so the bus took a detour. I arrived at 9.40.
compare: Did you say sorry, and say that you are going to be late?
Did you use was + -ing: I was sitting on the bus when …?
Did you say when you will probably arrive?
Did your record give the time, the place and what happened?

canDo: I can tell someone what happened, and react to a story: Oh no! What happened then?
I can say what was going on with was or were + -ing.
I can use past forms like taught, spent and hid.
I can read an incident record and a witness statement.
I can phone my manager about a problem and fill in an incident record.

reading.before: Look at the title and the first picture. What do you think went wrong? Who is in the story?
reading.talk: What went wrong in the story, and what was going on at the time? Tell a short story about a day when something went wrong for you. Write two or three sentences, or say them to Wehel.

quiz.q: I ___ for the bus when it started to rain.
While we ___ lunch, the fire alarm rang.
It was cold, so I ___ my warm coat.
The road was closed, so the bus took a ___ .
quiz.why: A detour is a longer way, because the usual road is closed.

quiz.q: My passport wasn't in my bag. Then I found it in my coat. I was so ___ !
quiz.why: Relieved: happy because the worry has gone.

quiz.q: Which past verb ends in a t sound?
quiz.why: After sh, -ed sounds like t: crashed.

quiz.q: A person who sees an incident is a ___ .
To open the door, ___ the green button, then wait.
quiz.why: An instruction starts with the verb: press.

quiz.q: I've ___ sent the form. It went this morning.
Take an umbrella. I think it ___ rain later.
quiz.why: A guess: I think + will + a verb.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the conversation in pairs. Then each learner tells a short You'll never guess what happened! story, and the others react: Oh no! What happened then?

Day 2: a chain story. One learner says what was going on (I was waiting for the lift …), and the next adds what happened (… when the lights went off). Then drill the past forms in pairs: teach, taught; spend, spent; hide, hid.
Day 3: the task. You are the manager, and each learner phones about a problem on the way to work. Then they fill in the incident record and read it aloud.
Day 4: talk about the book, answer questions, and read two learners' mornings that went wrong aloud.
